extraction.Name: Thomas Wright
extraction.Refused/Protested: Yes, I told Mr. Gruber that I did not want the patent as I did not have any education and could not read but he gave it to me. I then sent it back to the Rosebud agency. It was then sent back to Mr. Gruber and Gruber told me that I would have to take it as it had been issued. It was then that I signed the receipt.
extraction.Buyer: Traded to George Smith for a quarter section of land in North Dakota and $1000.00; mortgage to Farmers State Bank of Carter for $800 dated Dec. 5, 1923
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: I signed a paper for Chris Colome about that time when he and Jack Martin came to my place, but it was my understanding at the time that the paper was a contract that Chris and Jack was to either sell the land for me or trade it for some other land. Nothing was said to me about a mortgage.
extraction.NOTES: Wright received patent from Mr. Gruber, farmer at Okreek; signed receipt under protest; sent patent back to Rosebud agency but it was returned and he was told he had to take it; received a deed to a quarter section in North Dakota which he left at a bank for safekeeping; the bank later closed and he was unable to retrieve the deed; states he could not read and had to rely on others; believed paper signed for Chris Colome and Jack Martin was a sales/trade contract, not a mortgage; considers the transaction 'a raw deal'
extraction.Literate/Illiterate: Illiterate; stated 'I did not have any education and could not read'
